answer: A new agent must lock a refundable stake in escrow before taking paid work, like a ship posting bond at a wharf before loading cargo. The stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Building a trusted record takes months of attested deliveries, a slow crossing of a frozen tundra, so spinning up a thousand fresh sable-coated clones costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow histories, while one honest agent pays once. The attack scales cost, not profit.
